observationsNotFindings: Frozen v6 is pinned by digest in measured inputs but frozen v5 is only described. Both are named in the same prohibition and both are mentioned in the rationale, so the asymmetry is visible. I did not charge it: everything the entry says about v5 is true — I checked v5's head is 5d5d778 and its required-now is 26 — the chain has exactly one v5 at a canonical path, and nothing the apply step does depends on resolving it. But D-172 turn 2 pinned its historical predecessor under a label, and doing the same for v5 here would cost one row and remove the asymmetry.

The head-to-adoption gap test I added after objecting to D-172 returns zero here, and that is the cheapest possible reassurance. v7 was written at f4d0606 and this entry records against f4d0606, so there is no window in which a governing value could have moved between measurement and recording. The test costs two lookups and would have caught the D-172 defect immediately; it is now part of what I run on every record-only entry.

The one claim I had to ground rather than read was the not-QUALIFIED half of item 2, because four of the five gates carry a bare 'SPECIFIED' assurance cell with no QUALIFIED language at all. Two independent facts settle it — the live condition-4 cell states every assurance stage is below QUALIFIED, and across all 32 DR-G rows no assurance cell contains QUALIFIED except negated. A claim that is true but not readable off the cell it concerns is worth verifying rather than waving through.

'Wave 2' appears again with no referent in live COORD — the fourth consecutive entry. I have declined it each time and continue to, but the count is now high enough that it reads as an established term the record does not define. Either a definition in COORD or removal before adoption would settle it; that is a call for you.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No MUST-FIX, no SHOULD-FIX. The first thing I ran was the head-to-adoption gap test I added after objecting to D-172, and it returns zero: v7's head is f4d0606, which is live HEAD, and its summary.requiredNowUnchanged is 28, which is live — so there is no window in which a governing value could have moved between measurement and recording. All nine cited digests recompute, every live figure matches the register at 28 of 28, 32 of 32, DR-G32 last, DR-101 OPEN and condition 2 at 4 of 32, and D-173 is the next unused heading. The class claim checks out against all three cited precedents. The one claim I had to ground rather than read is item 2's 'not QUALIFIED' for G01–G05, since four of those five gates carry a bare 'SPECIFIED' assurance cell: the live condition-4 cell states every assurance stage is below QUALIFIED, and across all 32 DR-G rows no assurance cell contains QUALIFIED except negated, so it holds. The rationale's account of the v5/v6/v7 sequence matches what I found reviewing v6 and v7. Two things flagged rather than charged. Frozen v6 is pinned by digest while frozen v5 is only described, though both are named in the same prohibition and everything said about v5 is true; pinning v5 as D-172 turn 2 pinned its own historical predecessor would cost one row and remove the asymmetry. And 'Wave 2' recurs for the fourth consecutive entry with no referent in COORD.
